item.title: Canada's top court largely upholds Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants
item.description:
Closely watched decision exposes tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights Canada’s top court has largely upheld a controversial secularism law in the province of Quebec barring public sector workers from wearing conspicuous religious symbols, in a closely watched decision that exposes the tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights. In a 6-1 ruling released on Friday morning , the supreme court found Quebec was permitted to shield the law, Bill 21, from most court challenges on the grounds that it violated charter rights. item.title: Is Spain 'nostalgic' for Franco? Would traditional right PP consider an alliance with far-right Vox?
item.description:
Santiago Abascal’s party has adopted radical ideas from France and beyond. If it joins a PP coalition, it would be a morale boost for allies across the continent It was a scene few would have imagined possible in Spanish politics until recently. Flanked on stage by Catalan flags, the far-right Vox leader, Santiago Abascal, addressed a packed campaign rally in Girona, where he promised “to defend Catalan identity” against supposed “Islamisation”. He urged his audience to confront what he claimed was “the primary challenge” of a new “caliphate” across Spain. For a fringe party that made its breakthrough in 2018 by demonising Catalonia’s independence movement, it was a striking change of emphasis, reflecting a strategic shift that has brought Vox to the brink of power. item.title: Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy, halts flights and ticket sales
item.description:
A Norse Atlantic Airways Boeing 787. PATRICK T. FALLON/AFP via Getty Images Norse Atlantic's Norwegian operating unit filed for bankruptcy as it fights to stay in business. It also grounded its flights and received notices terminating the lease agreements for its fleet. Norse had been losing millions since fuel prices surged due to the Iran war. Cheap transatlantic flights are on the brink as Norse Atlantic filed for bankruptcy. The budget airline, which has previously offered one-way New York-to-London tickets for as little as $99, warned on Wednesday that its "financial situation is critical." On Friday, it announced that its Norwegian operating unit had filed for bankruptcy. All Norse flights are canceled, and ticket sales have been discontinued, it added. item.title: Open Thread
item.description:
People share food at the dinner table during Thanksgiving. —Stock photo—Getty Images As households across America prepare to gather for their Thanksgiving celebrations , there’s one question at the forefront of hosts’ minds: what time should dinner be served? A quick glance on social media will tell you that it’s a hotly-debated topic, and one that people have firm opinions on. Lifestyle expert Martha Stewart’s online publication conducted a poll in 2024, asking readers what time Thanksgiving dinner should start. More than 34,000 people joined the conversation, with the majority of respondents (13,586) saying the meal should begin between 2 to 3 p.m., local time. item.title: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town after army chief's threat sparks row
item.description:
Uganda's army on Friday said it planned to withdraw from the eastern DR Congo town of Lubero in North Kivu. The announcement came days after Ugandan army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba – son of President Yoweri Museveni – threatened to take control of Walikale, another North Kivu town, sparking a diplomatic spat between the two neighbouring nations.

item.title: Eastern US recovers from storms that snarled Thanksgiving travel as flooding continues
item.description:
Heavy rains and high winds downed trees and power lines and led to water rescues from New York to Virginia Skies are clearing along the US eastern seaboard, and power was being restored to hundreds of thousands of customers, whose Thanksgiving plans were disrupted by heavy rains and high winds that swept over the region on Thursday. The storms snarled travel, downed trees and power lines and led to water rescues from New York to Virginia. At its peak, nearly a million customers were without power and widespread coastal flooding was reported by Poweroutage.us. Continue reading...
